summary.text: Odysseus' cowherd on Ithaca, who like Eumaeus the swineherd kept faith through twenty years of absence and stood with the returned king when the suitors were slain.

story.text: Homer brings Philoetius to the halls with cattle for the wooers' feast: a leader of men driving a barren heifer and fat she-goats brought over from the mainland. He cursed the suitors who devoured another man's goods and prayed that Odysseus might yet return — and if he did, Philoetius would give him a cloak and tunic and send him safe to Dulichium.

When the beggar proved himself in the bow-contest and the slaughter began, Philoetius locked the outer gates with Eumaeus so none of the suitors could escape; he then fought in the hall beside Odysseus and Telemachus. When the kin of the slain rallied against the house, he armed at Laertes' side with Eumaeus.
